question: True or false: the hottest stars show the strongest hydrogen lines in their spectra?
answer: False. Hydrogen lines peak in white A-type stars near 10,000 K, like Vega. The visible lines need hydrogen atoms whose electron already sits one step up; hotter stars strip the electron off entirely, cooler ones leave it at the bottom. That is why the old alphabetical classes were reshuffled into O, B, A.
move: A signal that rises with its cause can fall when the cause goes further.
ask: Where do I assume more of a good thing always gives more of the effect?
trap: Assuming more heat always means a stronger hydrogen signal.
reference: Gray & Corbally, Stellar Spectral Classification, Princeton University Press, 2009
